capabilities.title: Choose LoRA rank, alpha, and target modules
capabilities.summary: Decision rules for LoraConfig: rank capacity trade-off, alpha = 2*rank scaling, and per-architecture target-module lists.

when: Configuring LoraConfig for a new LoRA or QLoRA fine-tuning run.
Fine-tuning quality is insufficient and adapter capacity may be the cause.

steps: Start at r=8 (recommended starting point) or r=16 (general fine-tuning); reserve r=32-64 for complex tasks, domain adaptation, or 70B-scale models.
Set lora_alpha = 2 * r as the default scaling; lower alpha is conservative, higher is aggressive.

Pick target_modules by architecture: Llama/Mistral/Qwen use q_proj,v_proj,k_proj,o_proj(,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj); GPT-2/GPT-Neo use c_attn,c_proj,c_fc; Falcon and BLOOM use query_key_value,dense,dense_h_to_4h,dense_4h_to_h; or use target_modules='all-linear' (PEFT 0.6.0+).
Target attention + MLP layers for the best quality/efficiency trade-off.

capabilities.title: Fine-tune with LoRA adapters on a single GPU
capabilities.summary: Attach LoRA adapters via get_peft_model and train ~0.1-1% of parameters with base weights frozen; save the small adapter instead of the full model.

when: Fine-tuning 7B-70B models on GPUs with limited memory (consumer GPUs, single A100).
Training <1% of parameters with minimal accuracy loss is acceptable.
Multiple task-specific fine-tuned variants are wanted from one base model.
avoid_when: Training small models (<1B parameters) — full fine-tuning is preferred.
Maximum quality is required and compute budget exists for full fine-tuning.
Significant domain shift requires updating all weights.

expected_outcomes: Adapter file is megabytes (e.g., ~6MB) instead of a multi-GB full model copy.
Trainable parameter fraction around 0.1-1% of the base model.

steps: Load the base model and tokenizer (torch_dtype='auto', device_map='auto'); set tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token if unset.
Build LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM, r=8-16, lora_alpha=2*r, lora_dropout~0.05, target_modules per architecture, bias='none').
Wrap the model with get_peft_model(model, lora_config).
Verify trainable parameters BEFORE training with model.print_trainable_parameters().
Tokenize the dataset (truncation, bounded max_length) and train with Trainer/TrainingArguments (fp16, gradient accumulation as needed).
Save only the adapter with model.save_pretrained(adapter_dir).

validation: model.print_trainable_parameters() reports a small trainable fraction (e.g., ~0.17% for Llama-3.1-8B at r=16), not 100%.
The saved adapter directory reloads via AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained.
Training loss is finite and decreasing.
recovery: CUDA OOM: enable model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(), or per_device_train_batch_size=1 with gradient_accumulation_steps=16, or switch to QLoRA (4-bit).
Adapter not applying: check model.active_adapters, model.print_trainable_parameters(), and that model.train() was called.
Quality degradation: increase r to 32 (alpha 64), target 'all-linear', use more data/epochs, or lower learning_rate to 1e-4.

capabilities.title: QLoRA: fine-tune a 4-bit quantized model when VRAM is the constraint
capabilities.summary: Load the base model in 4-bit (NF4, bf16 compute), call prepare_model_for_kbit_training, then attach LoRA — fits 70B-class models on a single 24GB GPU at a ~5% quality trade-off and ~0.84x training speed.

when: Memory is the primary constraint (e.g., fine-tuning a 70B model on a single 24GB GPU).
The model does not fit in available VRAM for standard fp16/bf16 LoRA fine-tuning.
A ~5% quality trade-off versus full fine-tuning is acceptable.
avoid_when: Available VRAM comfortably fits standard fp16/bf16 LoRA for the model size (e.g., an 8B model on a >=40GB GPU: LoRA needs ~18GB) — prefer standard LoRA: QLoRA trains slower (0.84x vs 1.3x relative to full fine-tuning) and costs additional quality (MMLU ~0.6-1.3 below LoRA).
Maximum quality is required and compute budget exists for full fine-tuning.

expected_outcomes: A 70B-class model becomes trainable on a single 24GB GPU.
QLoRA memory footprint ~6GB for an 8B model at r=16 (vs ~18GB fp16 LoRA).

steps: Build BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_compute_dtype='bfloat16', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True).
Load the base model with quantization_config=bnb_config and device_map='auto'.
Call prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model) BEFORE attaching adapters (enables gradient checkpointing).
Attach LoRA with get_peft_model, using a higher rank for very large models (e.g., r=64, lora_alpha=128 for 70B) targeting attention+MLP projections.
Verify trainable parameters, then train as in standard LoRA.

validation: prepare_model_for_kbit_training was applied before get_peft_model (matches the documented call order).
model.print_trainable_parameters() reports a small trainable fraction.
The quantized base + adapter fits within the target GPU memory budget.
recovery: CUDA OOM: enable gradient checkpointing and reduce batch size with higher gradient accumulation.

capabilities.title: Load, merge, or hot-swap trained adapters for deployment
capabilities.summary: Reload adapters via AutoPeftModelForCausalLM, merge into the base with merge_and_unload for adapter-free deployment, or serve multiple adapters (set_adapter / vLLM LoRARequest).

when: A trained adapter checkpoint needs to be deployed or evaluated.
Serving multiple task-specific adapter variants from one base model.
The inference stack needs a single merged, adapter-free model.
avoid_when: The adapter has not yet been evaluated on held-out data — evaluate before merging.

steps: Load directly with AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(adapter_dir, device_map='auto') (recommended), or PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, adapter_dir).
For adapter-free deployment: merged = model.merge_and_unload(); save merged model and tokenizer (save_pretrained / push_to_hub).
For multi-adapter serving: model.load_adapter(dir, adapter_name=...); switch with model.set_adapter(name); bypass with the model.disable_adapter() context.
For vLLM adapter serving: LLM(model=base, enable_lora=True) and pass LoRARequest(name, id, adapter_dir) per generate call.

validation: AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained succeeds on the saved adapter directory.
model.active_adapters shows the expected adapter name after set_adapter.
recovery: Adapter not applying: check model.active_adapters and model.print_trainable_parameters().

capabilities.title: PEFT method resource footprint and quality trade-offs
capabilities.summary: Measured memory/speed/quality comparisons across full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, and IA3, plus the method-selection table for PEFT variants.

when: Budgeting GPU memory before choosing a fine-tuning method.
Choosing among PEFT methods (LoRA/QLoRA/AdaLoRA/IA3/prefix/prompt tuning) for a task.
Estimating the training-throughput impact of quantized fine-tuning.

steps: Memory (Llama-3.1-8B): full fine-tuning 60+GB; LoRA r=16 ~18GB; QLoRA r=16 ~6GB; IA3 ~16GB.
Training speed (A100 80GB): LoRA ~1.3x of full fine-tuning throughput; QLoRA ~0.84x (slower than full FT).
Quality (MMLU, Llama-2 7B/13B): LoRA within ~0.5-0.6 points of full FT; QLoRA within ~1.2-1.3 points.

Method selection: LoRA for general fine-tuning; QLoRA when memory-constrained; IA3 for few-shot with minimal parameters (0.01%); prefix tuning for generation control; prompt tuning for simple task adaptation.
